proof_summary: Direct divisor-and-modular-power enumeration establishes each proposed value and excludes every smaller modulus, with the large final search pruned by the bound that every qualifying divisor \(d\mid k\) is unitary: writing \(k=dq\), the congruence forces \(d^{d-1}\equiv1\pmod q\), hence \(\gcd(d,q)=1\). A square-root divisor count discards moduli having fewer than ten unitary divisors, and direct modular computation handles the remaining candidates below \(2310\).
